c.tagline: Swedish-speaking island capital of Åland, all sailing ships, cycling, and Baltic archipelago calm.

taxi.fareNote: Uber has no meaningful presence; metered taxis are booked by phone (Taxi Åland) or picked up at ranks near the harbours and centre.

emergency.note: 112 is the single EU emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: The walkable heart of town around the Torggatan and Nygatan shopping streets and the linden-lined Esplanade, with shops, cafes, and the town hall; the natural base for first-timers.
The Western Harbour, Mariehamn's international ferry port and maritime showpiece, home to the four-masted barque Pommern and the Åland Maritime Museum; best for sights and sea history.
The Eastern Harbour, home to Sjökvarteret — a working boatbuilding quarter — one of Scandinavia's largest marinas, and a quieter waterside feel; good for a calmer, nautical stay.
A leafy residential peninsula south of the centre with quiet lanes, shoreline paths, and easy cycling; suits families and travelers wanting a relaxed local base.
The original village north of the centre where Mariehamn was founded, now a calm residential area with the Övernässtugan farmhouse; good for longer, low-key stays.

water.note: Tap water is excellent and safe to drink.

transit.hours: Ålandstrafiken regional buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM on weekdays, with reduced weekend service, radiating from central stops on Torggatan.
transit.note: Mariehamn is flat and famously bike-friendly — most people cycle. Green Ålandstrafiken buses (lines 1-5) connect the town to the rest of the main island, and taxis fill late-night gaps.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash to the driver or with a rechargeable travel card; single tickets start around €3.

transit.m: Taxi to the city centre (~5 min)
Several downtown hotels offer free airport pickup on request

tip.r: Service is included in prices; rounding up or leaving ~5-10% for good service is appreciated but not expected.
